text.p: Madge Networks NV said Monday it is offering breakthrough computer networking technology to speed the performance of capacity-contrained networks at far lower cost than existing router technology.

Madge said three years of research and development work had produced the industry's first product integrating the functions of both switching and routing packet into a single, hardware-based switching system.
The company said its 3LS third-layer switching module is first and only network device in the industry capable of simultaneous switching and routing at full network speed.

Routers are the essential equipment used to lash together subnetworks, or the individual segments that compose larger computer networks. Leading suppliers include Cisco Systems Inc, 3Com Corp and Bay Networks Inc.
But routers are not well-suited to handle the increasing amount of data-intensive voice, video and graphics information traveling over networks, many industry analysts agree.
Madge said the new 3LS, which is priced at $16,995 and available immediately, offers two to 10 times the performance of equivalent products from Cisco at under one-third the cost.

Madge said its combined switch-router product will remain compatible with exisiting router equipment, but allow networks to sidestep the bottlenecks that can plague computer networks, sometimes bringing communications traffic grinding to a halt.
It said the 3LS roughly doubles overall network performance by eliminating bottlenecks caused by routers.

Madge said the 3LS transforms its core LANswitch product into a multilayer IP/IPX switch, capable of switching Internet traffic at rates up to one million data packets per second on Ethernet and Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) networks.

Madge said it has combined switching and routing technologies into a single application-specific (ASIC) computer chip, an inherently more efficient system in terms of speed and cost than hybrid software and hardware approaches.
The existing hybrid approach leads to performance bottlenecks because it relies on microprocessors that are not optimized for networking tasks.
Madge said the combined switch/router product is a crucial component of the MadgeOne architecture, first announced in mid-1996, for integrating data, voice and video.

The company said its breakthrough hardware product enables it to deliver systems with higher performance at far lower cost than conventional routers, without sacrificing the security or management controls provided by routers.
In addition, Madge said it will provide Internet switch/routing systems in the second half of 1997 based on high-speed network backbone technology.
The systems will support emerging standards for delivery multimedia voice video and data in ATM switches, ATM adapter cards and ATM edge switches for Ethernet and Token Ring.
Madge is headquartered in Amsterdam, but its stock is mainly traded in the United States on Nasdaq.
